history: Taichung, old 'Dadun', was chosen by Liu Mingchuan for a new walled city when Taiwan became a province in the Qing era — hence 'Taiwanfu'. Under Japanese rule it got a chessboard street plan, the first planned city on the island. Spring-like all year, it is called the most livable city. Bubble tea was born here (Chun Shui Tang, 1987); Fengjia Night Market leads Taiwan's night-market culture; Gaomei Wetland sunsets, the Rainbow Village paintings and Luce Chapel's curves keep visitors lingering.
importance: Hub of central Taiwan · A most livable city
unis: Grew from a Taichung agriculture school; tops Taiwan in agricultural and life sciences.
Taiwan's first TCM university — a leader in integrated Chinese-Western medicine.
Named after Qiu Fengjia; strong in business and engineering, with the famous Fengjia Night Market outside.
Taiwan's first private university — the I.M. Pei-designed Luce Chapel is its landmark.
From the Taichung normal school — a century of teacher education.
Its dentistry is famed island-wide; the hospital serves central Taiwan.
A Catholic university known for languages and tourism, with a beautiful tree-lined campus.
A modernist campus with an Asia University museum of Tadao Ando's triangle buildings.
A tech university of business roots, rich in tourism and culinary internships.
A private-donation-first example with deep mechanical engineering traditions.
Started in nursing; known for food nutrition and beauty design.
Design and finance both strong — next door to Rainbow Village.
foods: Chun Shui Tang invented pearl milk tea in 1987 — every hand-shaken tea in the world started here.
Malt-crisp pastry thin as paper — a Taichung city card for sixty years.
Fengjia Night Market's charcoal sausage wrapped in sticky rice — the queue says it all.
Transparent sweet-potato skin wrapped around bamboo and pork, steamed then fried, with sweet chili sauce.
Taichung is the pineapple-cake homeland — Sunrise turned it into a boutique treat.
Xing Fa Ting's honey-bean ice, ninety years old — a hill of candied beans and fruits.
Yizhong Street's wild creation — fried noodles inside a hot bun, double carb joy.
Purple mille-feuille of Dajia taro, dense taro paste inside, deeply fragrant.
A classic of central night markets — the iron-shovel old shop of Zhongxiao Street, thirty seconds to serve.
Sugar & Nut nougat by Tunghai University — a must-buy for international travelers.
scenes: A boardwalk reaches into the wind; at sunset the whole wetland turns golden mirror.
Grandpa Huang's rainbow paintings saved the whole military village — world visitors come to see it.
The curved double-shell chapel by I.M. Pei and Chen Chi-kwan — the soul of Tunghai University.
A century-old park opened in 1903 — the Lake Pavilion is a Japanese-era landmark.
Ito Toyo's 'sound-carrying curves' — among the hardest buildings ever built.
Taiwan's most popular night market — new snacks spread from here island-wide.
A hidden valley under Xueshan — February cherry blossoms with the peak in postcard light.
A hot-spring village on the Central Cross-Island Highway — soft springs, grand valley views.
A 3.6-km green belt linking the art museum and shops — best for a stroll or ride.
Twelve boardwalk trails over twelve hills — the 'balcony of Taichung'.
